anime_title: Even the Student Council Has Its Holes!
episode_title: Deadpan Chaos and the Art of the Snappy Gag
pullquote: Passione proves once again that top-tier comedy lives or dies on razor-sharp cuts, and Episode 3 hits the gas pedal right when the council room starts unspooling into pure, unfiltered nonsense.
quick_take: Passione proves once again that top-tier comedy lives or dies on razor-sharp cuts, and Episode 3 hits the gas pedal right when the council room starts unspooling into pure, unfiltered nonsense.
one_sentence_verdict: If you want an ecchi slice-of-life comedy where the timing is sharper than a razor and the cast refuses to behave normally for even five seconds, Episode 3 is mandatory late-night watching.
synopsis_paragraphs: That sudden smack of deadpan silence right after a punchline drops is where this show strikes gold. Episode 3 throws you straight into the messy, claustrophobic swirl of the student council room, and the energy does not let up for a single breath. The comedy here isn't just delivering manga panels on screen; it is all about weaponized comedic momentum. You get these wild tonal shifts where high-strung panic crashes headfirst into absolute, unbothered lethargy.

What makes it land is the confidence in the craft. Instead of drowning out every beat with wall-to-wall background tracks, the episode knows exactly when to drop everything so you can hear a pin drop—or rather, hear the awkward breathing of characters who just realized they stepped way over the line. Ume is fighting for his academic life, yet the sheer gravitational pull of this bizarre crew drags him into one ridiculous corner after another. You can feel the staff having an absolute blast tweaking the frame rates and exaggerating the small micro-expressions before snapping back to picture-perfect character sheets. It is loud, it is shameless, and it keeps you grinning the entire run.
sakuga_paragraphs:
- **Visual snap and deformation:** Director Naoyuki Tatsuwa and the animation team keep the visual rhythm snappy by slamming sudden chibi exaggerations against Ryou Imamura's wonderfully expressive, clean character designs, making every sudden physical reaction hit like a miniature slapstick grenade.
- **Audio drops and room silence:** Sound Director Satoshi Motoyama knows that the funniest sound in high-speed comedy is sudden, dead silence; muting Tomoki Kikuya's percussive soundtrack right before a character reacts lets the sheer absurdity of the student council room linger in the air just long enough to sting.
story_paragraphs:
- **「テンポ良すぎて草」 (The comedic tempo is way too good, lol):** A constant refrain across late-night 5ch threads and X feeds whenever an episode barrels through four distinct council room misunderstandings without letting the viewer take a breath.
- **「ツッコミが追いつかない」 (The straight-man comebacks can't even keep up):** Dropped across live-reaction boards to describe how Ume gets completely buried by the chaotic antics of Hisako, Tan, and Komaro, leaving the audience just as breathless as the protagonist.
voice_paragraphs: - **Deadpan contrast in the booth:** Shougo Sakata plays Ume with the exact brand of exhausted, grounded straight-man energy needed to anchor the madness, giving Haruka Shiraishi (Hisako Kotobuki) and Miyu Tomita (Komaro Michinoku) the perfect brick wall to bounce their chaotic, hyperactive cadences off of without missing a single comedic beat.
takeaway_paragraphs: If you want an ecchi slice-of-life comedy where the timing is sharper than a razor and the cast refuses to behave normally for even five seconds, Episode 3 is mandatory late-night watching. Catch the official stream right now over on Bilibili TV.
